edition.locus: Gebhardt XIII.V (hung by the thumbs; growth in God)

source_text: Tunc attentantur numerosis durisque cruciatibus per stationarium militem, iustorum piorumque carnificem, adhibitis in auxilium crudelitatis eius centurione et Cirtensium magistratibus. Hoc est diaboli sacerdotibus, tanquam membrorum laceratione frangeretur fides, cui cura corporis uilis est. Et Iacobus quidem, sicuti erat in uirtute fidei semper austerior, qui et infestationes iam semel Decianae persecutionis euicerat, affectauit se non Christianum tantum, sed et diaconum confiteri. Marianum autem tormentis fecit obnoxium, quod se lectorem tantum, sicuti fuerat, fatebatur. Quaenam illa tormenta! Quam noua, quam diaboli uenenato sensu et deiciendi artibus exquisita supplicia! Pependit Marianus ad uulnera, eoque martyri etiam in ipsis lacerationibus suis affuit gratia, sic torsus est, ut illum exaltaret et poena. Nexus autem qui pendentem gerebant, non manus, sed summos apices pollicum uinxerant, scilicet ut digitorum tenuis exilitas plus in ferendis membris ceteris laboraret. Addita etiam pedibus iniusta pondera, ut dum discordantibus poenis utrimque distracta et uiscerum conuulsione resoluta, de neruis suis totius corporis compago penderet. Nihil egisti iuxta dei templum, iuxta Christi coheredem, nequitia gentilis. Suspenderis licet membra, concusseris latera, diuulseris uiscera, Marianus noster in deum fidens, quantum corpore, tantum et mente crescebat. Uicta denique feritate torquentium, rursus in carcerem de triumpho suo multum laetatus includitur. Ibi cum Iacobo et ceteris fratribus gaudium uictoriae dominicae frequenti oratione celebrauit.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: then they are assailed by many severe tortures through a station-soldier, killer of just and godly men, with a centurion and the magistrates of Cirta added to help his cruelty; this is by priests of the devil, as though faith, for which concern for the body is worthless, might be broken by mangling of limbs; and James, being always sterner in strength of faith, who had already once before defeated the attacks of the Decian persecution, strove to profess himself not only Christian but also deacon; but Marian's admitting himself only lector, as he had been, made him exposed to torments; what torments, how novel, how sought out by the devil's poisoned mind and skills of overthrow; Marian hung for wounding, and grace attended the martyr even in his lacerations, for he was racked so that even punishment raised him up; the ties holding him hanging bound not his hands but the top tips of his thumbs, so that the thin slightness of his fingers would labor more in carrying the other limbs; also unfair weights were added to his feet, so that while pulled apart on both sides by disagreeing pains and loosened by convulsion of entrails, the frame of his whole body hung from its sinews; pagan evil, you did nothing against God's temple, against Christ's co-heir; though you suspend limbs, shake sides, tear entrails, our Marian, trusting in God, increased as much in mind as in body; finally with the torturers' fierceness defeated, he is shut again in prison, much rejoicing over his triumph; there with James and the other brothers he celebrated the joy of the Lord's victory in constant prayer.
pass_b_english: Then they were assailed with numerous and harsh torments by the soldier on his post, a butcher of just and holy men, with a centurion and the magistrates of Cirta taken to himself to aid his cruelty. This was done by priests of the devil, as if faith, for whom care of the body is a cheap thing, could be broken by the laceration of limbs. And James, since he was always the sterner in the strength of his faith, who had also already once overcome the assaults of the Decian persecution, pressed to confess himself not only a Christian but also a deacon. But Marian was made subject to torments because he acknowledged himself to be only a lector, as he had been. What torments those were. How new, how carefully devised by the devil's poisoned mind and his arts of casting down were those punishments. Marian hung stretched out for wounding, and grace stood by the martyr even in the midst of his own lacerations, for he was racked in such a way that even his punishment lifted him on high. The bonds that bore him as he hung had bound not his hands but the topmost tips of his thumbs, so that the thin slenderness of his fingers would labor the more in carrying the other members. Unjust weights were also added to his feet, so that, while he was dragged apart on both sides by discordant pains and loosened by the wrenching of his inward parts, the frame of his whole body hung from its own sinews.

You accomplished nothing, pagan wickedness, against the temple of God (1 Corinthians 6:19), against the co-heir of Christ (Romans 8:17). Though you suspend his limbs, shake his sides, and tear his inward parts asunder, our Marian, trusting in God, grew in mind as much as he was strained in body. At last, when the savagery of those who tortured him was conquered, he was shut up again in prison, rejoicing greatly over his triumph. There with James and the other brothers he celebrated the joy of the Lord's victory with constant prayer.

choices.why: stationarius is functional, a soldier assigned to a guard post, not merely standing still
iniusta keeps the moral judgment of the narrator against an unjust imbalance, not only physical unevenness

rejected: next to the temple of God
